title: The earth
hookLine: why some Hindus ask the earth's pardon before their feet touch the floor: the Prithvi Sukta and the earth as a shared mother
tomorrow: two schools argued over what to sing to a bride. who won?

lines: AN ALARM, A PHONE, FEET ON THE FLOOR.
A VERSE BEFORE THE FIRST STEP.
cards: An alarm. A phone already in hand. Feet on the floor before the eyes are fully open.

Some Hindus pause right there. Before their feet touch the ground, they say a short Sanskrit verse to the earth, and it ends with an apology: forgive me for touching you with my feet. Saying sorry to a floor.
That's the odd detail. Why would anyone ask the ground's pardon for standing on it?

teach.b: The verse is a traditional morning prayer, and it speaks to the earth as a goddess: clothed in the oceans, the wife of Vishnu. Hindus call her Bhudevi.
Nobody can live without stepping on her, so you greet her first and ask her pardon. And the idea has a scripture behind it. The Atharva Veda has a long hymn to the earth, the Prithvi Sukta.
In one verse the singer says the earth is his mother and he is her son.

In another, the earth carries people of many languages and many customs, each in their own home. So here's the puzzle solved. In this Hindu teaching, the earth isn't a backdrop, and she isn't simply property.
She's a mother you live on, and everyone else lives on her too. You don't trash your mother's house, and you aren't her only child.

One to tell a friend tonight: some classical Indian dancers touch the floor before they dance, asking the earth's pardon for the stamping to come. A pope, writing as a Christian, reached for a close picture.
Pope Francis subtitled his letter on the environment: on care for our common home.

how: Some Hindus say a short Sanskrit morning verse to the earth (Samudra vasane devi) before stepping out of bed, touching the ground and then their forehead. The Prithvi Sukta of the Atharva Veda is recited as a hymn to the earth.

the soil a gardener plants in
a resource each owner can use as they like

games.q: your roommate leaves the tap running while brushing and says the water bill is tiny anyway. what does the Hindu picture of the earth add?
o: it isn't about the bill: the water belongs to a mother everyone shares
nothing; saving water only matters when it saves money

games.why: the morning verse doesn't stop anyone stepping; it asks them to step with respect. in the Prithvi Sukta, the earth is mother to many peoples at once.

practice: Put your palm flat on the floor, or on the ground if you're outside. Feel that it's holding you up right now, and holding everyone else too.
Keep your hand there while you breathe, and choose one thing you'll stop throwing away this week.

wordCard.voice: The earth: in Hindu teaching, Bhudevi, a mother who carries people of every language. The floor under you is her house, and theirs.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the earth, as in the Prithvi Sukta, the Atharva Veda's hymn to her.

carryVoice: Keep this: the common home, one earth carrying everyone, greeted with an apology each morning. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Traditional Sanskrit morning verse to the earth (Samudra vasane devi parvata stana mandale, Vishnu patni namas tubhyam, pada sparsham kshamasva me)
Atharva Veda 12.1.12 (the earth as mother, I her son) and 12.1.45 (the earth bears people of many tongues and customs)
Pope Francis, Laudato si', subtitle 'on care for our common home'
